new_issues.description: Table tab:secondary reports a median signed log2 gap of -21.96 for cosine directional dispersion under the shared threshold, i.e. a ratio near 2^-22. That is a numerical artefact of taking log2 ratios of a quantity that is essentially zero at consensus (cosine admits almost all pairs in the unit cube). So the log2 scale, the median and the +-0.25 equivalence count are ill-defined for directional dispersion (and possibly radial spread) whenever runs reach consensus. Nothing in the text or the caption says so.

new_issues.non_match_rationale: R11/R3 ask that secondary outcomes be reported under every rule, and they are; this issue is about whether one reported number is valid (a log ratio near zero), which no roadmap criterion covers.

new_issues.description: The new definitions of radial spread (variance of opinion lengths) and directional dispersion (one minus the length of the mean unit opinion vector) measure from the origin. By the paper's own origin box, these are origin-dependent outcomes, yet the text does not say in which coordinates they are computed (the primary outcome is explicitly measured in centred coordinates). Terminology is also inconsistent across outputs: 'radial spread' and 'directional dispersion' in the text and Table tab:secondary, but 'radial var' and 'dispersion' in Tables tab:crossing and tab:crossing-run; neither term is in the glossary.

new_issues.non_match_rationale: S1/R11 require the measures to be defined and reported separately, which is done. This issue is that the definitions themselves fall under the paper's own origin-dependence warning and leave the coordinate frame unstated, which no roadmap item asks about.
